items.title: OpenAI tests Private Inference with a small group of customers
items.takeaway: Altman says Private Inference, part of OpenAI Private Intelligence, adds stronger privacy for business work.
items.soWhat: Privacy terms are becoming a product tier; ask your AI vendors which protections you actually have.

items.title: Claude agent teams helped Anthropic rewrite its API from Python to Rust
items.takeaway: The old Python service served as the reference; agents found and fixed differences in the new one.
items.soWhat: Keep the old system as the test reference and agents can take on large rewrites.

items.title: swyx warns cost-per-task charts can hide model reliability problems
items.takeaway: He highlights the view that human attention, not token cost, is the scarce resource.
items.soWhat: Judge agents by how much review time they save, not only by price per task.

items.title: Amazon reportedly in talks to stop blocking Meta's Muse shopping agent
items.takeaway: The Verge reports Amazon may end its block on Meta's Muse AI shopping agent.
items.soWhat: Retailers are deciding whether AI agents can shop for customers; set your own policy early.

items.title: Lenny's 25-task benchmark puts Gemini 4 Neon ahead of GPT-6.2 and Claude
items.takeaway: Lenny's Newsletter reports Gemini 4 Neon beat GPT-6.2 and Claude in its own 25-task benchmark.
items.soWhat: Run your own task benchmark before switching; public rankings keep changing week to week.

items.title: Jensen Huang tells Nvidia staff Trump did not get him rehired
items.takeaway: The Verge reports Huang told staff it is 'not true' that Trump got him rehired.
items.soWhat: Nvidia's leadership story is not settled; watch it if your AI plans rely on its chips.

voices.quote: Cost per task is a misleading metric; the scarce resource is human attention, not token cost
